assets.title: Retail 1: Cognigy AI Agent
assets.summary: A shopper on a fashion retail site is handled entirely by the Cognigy AI agent in web chat: store opening hours, the returns policy, a product recommendation returned as rich cards with View Details and View Product buttons, adding to cart and buying, and finally a damaged item, which is the point at which the AI decides to hand over to a human. Silent, with narration captions on screen rather than a voice over.

chapters.label: Opening title
chapters.talkTrack: This is the first of eight, and it stays entirely on the customer side. Nothing here has reached a human yet.

chapters.label: Opening hours, answered 24/7
chapters.talkTrack: A simple question first, deliberately. The point being made is availability: this costs the same at three in the morning as it does at midday.

chapters.label: Returns policy from the knowledge base
chapters.talkTrack: The answer is coming out of the knowledge base rather than being generated freely, which is what keeps it on-brand and stops it inventing a policy.

chapters.label: Several intents in one conversation
chapters.talkTrack: Watch that the shopper changes subject and the agent follows. Most bots are one question and done, and this is where that difference shows.

chapters.label: Taking action, not just answering
chapters.talkTrack: Here it stops talking and starts doing: it is connected to the tools behind the site, so it can complete the task rather than describe it.

chapters.label: Rich cards and add to cart
chapters.talkTrack: These product cards are xApps. Self-service does not have to be a wall of text, and for retail that matters more than in most industries.

chapters.label: Damaged item, and the handover decision
chapters.talkTrack: And this is the moment worth pausing on. It recognises this one is not for it, and hands over. Knowing when to stop is as important as the containment rate.

talkingPoints: 24/7 availability with no incremental cost, containment at scale without additional headcount
Knowledge base guardrails ensure accurate, on-brand, compliant responses every time
Agentic AI handles multiple intents within a single conversation, not just one and done
Connected to tools to execute processes end-to-end without human involvement
xApps deliver rich, interactive self-service experiences beyond simple text responses
Intelligent escalation decisions: AI knows when to resolve and when to hand over

assets.title: Retail 2: CXone Agent
assets.summary: The human agent side of the same retail conversation, in CXone Agent. The agent picks up the escalated shopper with Copilot alongside them in App Space: suggested replies, knowledge, sentiment, and a wrap-up. The claims made on screen are about agent economics, handle time, onboarding time and attrition, rather than about features. Silent, with narration captions on screen.

chapters.label: The agent picks up
chapters.talkTrack: This is the other half of clip one. Same conversation, now on the agent desktop.

chapters.label: Real-time assistance and auto-wrap
chapters.talkTrack: The claim on screen is a fifteen to twenty-five percent cut in handle time, and it is coming from two places: help during the call, and the wrap-up being written for them afterwards.

chapters.label: Onboarding and consistency
chapters.talkTrack: This is the argument that lands best with anyone running a seasonal operation. New starters reach competency in weeks rather than months, because the guidance is in the tool.

chapters.label: Agent effort and retention
chapters.talkTrack: Worth naming the second-order effect: lower cognitive load is a retention argument, not just a productivity one. In retail contact centres attrition is usually the bigger number.

chapters.label: Sentiment coaching in the moment
chapters.talkTrack: Coaching arrives while it can still change the outcome, instead of in a review three weeks later.

chapters.label: Schedule, evaluations and coaching in one place
chapters.talkTrack: And the agent sees their own schedule, evaluations and coaching here too, so none of it is happening to them out of sight.

talkingPoints: Average Handle Time reductions of 15-25% through real-time AI assistance and auto-wrap
Faster agent onboarding: new starters reach competency in weeks, not months, with AI as their guide
Consistent quality across the entire team regardless of tenure or experience level
Reduced agent effort and lower cognitive load translates directly to improved retention
In-the-moment sentiment coaching replaces retrospective feedback, so behaviour changes faster
Agents empowered with visibility of their schedule, evaluations, and coaching in one unified space

assets.title: Retail 3: CXone AI Studio
assets.summary: The shortest of the eight, and the one aimed at whoever will own the thing after go-live. CXone AI Studio is where the AI behaviour behind the retail scenario is configured, tested against live interactions before release, and kept inside guardrails. The argument is that the business changes it, not the vendor and not a change request to IT. Silent, with narration captions on screen.

chapters.label: Business-owned configuration
chapters.talkTrack: The claim here is ownership. Whoever runs the operation changes the AI, without a vendor ticket and without waiting on an IT release.

chapters.label: Changing behaviour in minutes
chapters.talkTrack: This is the one that matters in retail specifically. Promotions and policies change weekly, so the AI has to change on that cadence too.

chapters.label: Testing prompts against live interactions
chapters.talkTrack: And this is the safety net. Changes get tested against real interactions before they reach production, which is the answer to the obvious objection about letting the business edit the AI.

chapters.label: Guardrails and compliance controls
chapters.talkTrack: Guardrails are configured here rather than hoped for. Useful to note for anyone whose risk function will ask what stops it going off-script.

talkingPoints: Business-owned AI configuration: no vendor dependency, no IT bottleneck for updates
Rapid change cycles: update AI behaviour in minutes when policies or products change
Prompt testing against live interactions eliminates risk before changes go into production
Guardrails and compliance controls built in, so AI stays within defined boundaries at all times

assets.title: Retail 4: Copilot for Supervisors
assets.summary: Ninety seconds on the supervisor layer over the retail operation. Copilot for Supervisors surfaces live sentiment signals so a supervisor can intervene before a poor experience becomes a complaint, whisper-coach an agent mid-conversation, and spend their time developing people instead of listening in. The shortest and most focused of the eight. Silent, with narration captions on screen.

chapters.label: Managing larger teams
chapters.talkTrack: The headline claim is span of control: more agents per supervisor without losing the quality of oversight.

chapters.label: Intervening before it becomes a complaint
chapters.talkTrack: This is the proactive bit. The intervention happens while the conversation is still recoverable, rather than after a complaint arrives.

chapters.label: Acting on now, not last week
chapters.talkTrack: Sentiment signals are live. The contrast being drawn is with a report on Monday about what went wrong on Friday.

chapters.label: Whisper coaching
chapters.talkTrack: Whisper coaching, in the moment. Same argument as the agent clip, from the other side of the desk.

chapters.label: Supervisor time redirected
chapters.talkTrack: And the closing point is where the time goes. Less passive monitoring, more actual development of the team.

talkingPoints: Supervisors can effectively manage larger teams without sacrificing quality of oversight
Proactive intervention before a poor customer experience becomes a complaint or churn event
Sentiment signals allow supervisors to act on what's happening now, not what happened last week
Whisper coaching in the moment is more effective than retrospective feedback sessions
Supervisor time reclaimed from passive monitoring and redirected into genuine development activity

assets.title: Retail 5: CXone Interactions Hub
assets.summary: Interactions Hub as the single place every retail interaction lands, whatever channel it came in on. Shows synchronised call and screen playback for full context on an interaction, and a quality evaluation triggered in one click straight from playback rather than in a separate tool. The argument is consolidation: one recording estate instead of several. Silent, with narration captions on screen.

chapters.label: Every channel in one estate
chapters.talkTrack: The phrase they use is no dark corners: every channel recorded in one place, which is usually not the starting position.

chapters.label: Cost of multiple recording systems
chapters.talkTrack: This is the commercial argument, and it is the one procurement will care about: several disconnected recording systems collapse into one.

chapters.label: Synchronised call and screen playback
chapters.talkTrack: Call and screen together. You can see what the agent was actually doing, not just hear what was said, which is often where the real cause is.

chapters.label: One-click evaluation from playback
chapters.talkTrack: And the evaluation is triggered from here, in the same screen. No switching tools, no losing your place.

talkingPoints: Complete omnichannel visibility: no dark corners in your interaction estate
Significant cost and complexity reduction versus managing multiple disconnected recording systems
Synchronised call and screen playback gives the full context of every agent interaction
One-click QM evaluation triggers directly from playback: no system switching, no lost context

assets.title: Retail 6: CXone Quality Management
assets.summary: The longest of the eight, on automated quality management for the retail operation. Custom categories and behaviours encode the retailer's own standard, AI scores every interaction rather than a sample, prompts are validated against live interactions before deployment, and the QA team moves from manual scoring to exception management and calibration. Carries the strongest quantified claim in the set: 100% coverage against an industry norm of 1-3%. Silent, with narration captions on screen.

chapters.label: Your standard, not a generic one
chapters.talkTrack: Custom categories and behaviours first. The scoring reflects this retailer's standard rather than a template, which is usually the first objection from a QA lead.

chapters.label: Removing evaluator bias
chapters.talkTrack: AI scoring takes out evaluator bias and the calibration drift between assessors. Anyone who has run calibration sessions will recognise the problem being solved.

chapters.label: Validating before deployment
chapters.talkTrack: Same safety net as AI Studio: the scoring prompts get tested against live interactions before they go live.

chapters.label: 100% coverage versus 1-3%
chapters.talkTrack: This is the number to stop on. Every interaction scored, against an industry norm of one to three percent with manual QA. It changes what quality management is for.

chapters.label: What the QA team does instead
chapters.talkTrack: And that is the honest answer to what happens to the QA team: they move to exceptions, calibration and insight, rather than scoring forms all day.

talkingPoints: Custom categories, behaviours, and auto-response rules ensure your standard is precisely reflected
AI scoring eliminates evaluator bias and calibration inconsistency across your QA team
Prompt testing against live interactions validates AI accuracy before production deployment
100% interaction coverage versus the industry average of 1-3% with manual QA
QA teams shift from manual scoring to exception management, calibration, and strategic insight

assets.title: Retail 7: CXone Interaction Analytics
assets.summary: Interaction Analytics across every retail conversation rather than a hand-picked sample. Topic AI categorises automatically, so problems surface that nobody thought to search for; trends and anomalies appear at business speed rather than in a report weeks later; and you can drill from a trend line down to the transcript that caused it. Framed as much for product and marketing teams as for the contact centre. Silent, with narration captions on screen.

chapters.label: Every conversation, not a sample
chapters.talkTrack: Topic AI reads all of them. Same coverage argument as quality management, applied to insight rather than scoring.

chapters.label: Problems you did not know to look for
chapters.talkTrack: This is the part people underestimate. Automatic categorisation finds the thing you would never have written a search for.

chapters.label: Trends and anomalies at business speed
chapters.talkTrack: The contrast being drawn is with a monthly report. For a retailer mid-promotion, weeks later is the same as never.

chapters.label: Beyond the contact centre
chapters.talkTrack: Worth flagging who else this is for. Product, operations and marketing get customer intelligence out of it, which is often how the business case gets funded.

chapters.label: Reducing repeat contacts
chapters.talkTrack: And the operational payoff: find the underlying cause of contact volume and remove it, rather than staffing up to absorb it.

chapters.label: Drill from trend to transcript
chapters.talkTrack: Finally, the drill-through. Trend to transcript in a couple of clicks, so you get the actual cause rather than a metric that moved.

talkingPoints: 100% interaction coverage: Topic AI analyses every conversation, not a hand-picked sample
Automatic categorisation means you discover problems you didn't know to look for
Trend spotting and anomaly detection at the speed your business needs, not weeks later in a report
Product, operations, and marketing teams gain real customer intelligence to drive business decisions
Reduce repeat contacts by identifying and eliminating the underlying causes of contact volume
Drill-through from trend to transcript gives true root cause, not surface-level metrics

assets.title: Retail 8: CXone Actions
assets.summary: The last of the eight, and not what the name suggests: CXone Actions is unified BI across the whole CXone suite, queried in natural language so a business leader can ask a data question without an analyst. Automated Insights then reads real conversation patterns to identify which automation opportunities are actually worth building, sized by volume, and a Cognigy agent can be created from one in a click. Closes the loop from insight to deployed automation. Silent, with narration captions on screen.

chapters.label: Unified BI across the suite
chapters.talkTrack: One place for the whole suite's data. If someone has asked how these products report together, this is the answer.

chapters.label: Asking in natural language
chapters.talkTrack: And it is queried in plain language, which is the part that takes insight out of the analyst queue and puts it in front of whoever actually owns the number.

chapters.label: Automated Insights finds the opportunities
chapters.talkTrack: Now it turns predictive. It reads real conversation patterns and tells you where automation would pay, rather than you guessing.

chapters.label: Evidence, not gut feel
chapters.talkTrack: This is the slide to remember for a business case. Automation candidates ranked by evidence and volume, not by whoever argued loudest.

chapters.label: One click to a Cognigy agent
chapters.talkTrack: And then it closes the loop: build the Cognigy agent for that opportunity from here. Insight to deployed automation without a project in between.

talkingPoints: Unified BI across the entire CXone suite: one place for all your contact centre intelligence
Natural language querying puts data insight in the hands of every business leader, not just analysts
Spot trends, ask data questions in natural language, and zero in on process, CX, and knowledge gaps
Automated Insights identifies automation opportunities using AI analysis of real conversation patterns
Evidence-based automation decisions: not gut feel, but data-driven identification of the right use cases
One-click Cognigy agent creation collapses the time from insight to deployed automation

assets.title: CXone Agent Copilot
assets.summary: A human agent handles a life insurance application on a live voice call while Agent Copilot works alongside them: summarising the customer journey, flagging missing health questions, confirming identity checks, creating the application in Salesforce, requesting the physician statement, and drafting the reply for the agent to review.

chapters.label: Agents on high-value work
chapters.talkTrack: Quick framing before the product appears. The premise is that the human agent keeps the conversation and the judgement calls, and Copilot takes the administrative work around them.

chapters.label: The agent's screen
chapters.talkTrack: Here is the real workspace. Inbox on the left, a life insurance application in the middle, and Copilot in the App Space on the right. Watch the right-hand panel, that is where everything happens.

chapters.label: Copilot acts without being asked
chapters.talkTrack: Two things just landed on their own. Identity was verified against knowledge base authentication and external checks, and the application was created in Salesforce with an e-signature link already sent to the customer.

chapters.label: Next steps and a drafted reply
chapters.talkTrack: Now it has requested the physician statement, notified the underwriter, and drafted the response for the agent. Notice the agent is reviewing and sending, not composing from scratch.

chapters.label: What got automated
chapters.talkTrack: This is the summary of the work that happened in the background: creating the application, collecting the signature, chasing the medical record.

chapters.label: Close
chapters.talkTrack: The question worth sitting with is how much of that your agents currently do by hand, and what that costs you in handle time.

talkingPoints: Copilot works alongside the human agent in the App Space, it does not replace them
Demonstrates a live voice call on a life insurance new-business application
Shows identity verification, CRM record creation in Salesforce, and an e-signature request triggered without the agent doing it manually
Shows a drafted customer response that the agent reviews rather than writes
On-screen data is a demo environment, not a customer benchmark

assets.title: Retail: the voice AI agent
assets.summary: The voice counterpart to the retail chat clips, and the one that shows the Cognigy build alongside the call. A shopper phones NiCE Retail and speaks to a voice AI agent called Neil: opening hours, then the status of a specific order read back item by item with the total, then cancelling that order, then a question about tuxedos for a Christmas party. When the caller asks for a human, the agent hands over with a written Agentic Transfer Summary of the whole call, which is the part worth pausing on. The Cognigy flow and its live test panel are on screen throughout.

chapters.label: The call opens
chapters.talkTrack: A real phone call on the left, and the Cognigy flow that is driving it on the right. Useful for a technical audience, because you can see the tool calls fire as he speaks.

chapters.label: Order status, read back in detail
chapters.talkTrack: Listen to the level of detail here: both line items, the order date and the total, read back accurately. That is a live system lookup, not a canned response.

chapters.label: Cancelling the order
chapters.talkTrack: And now it acts on the account rather than describing how to. This is the difference between an IVR and an agent.

chapters.label: A product question, answered from knowledge
chapters.talkTrack: Then a completely different intent, tuxedos for a Christmas party, answered from the product knowledge base in the same call.

chapters.label: Handover with an Agentic Transfer Summary
chapters.talkTrack: This is the moment to stop on. The human agent does not arrive cold: they get a written summary of the whole call, the order number, and what the customer still needs.

assets.title: NiCE Homes: a voice assistant for lettings and property management
assets.summary: A vertical nothing else in the room covers. NiCE Homes is a fictional lettings agency managing rental property across Greater Manchester, with a voice assistant for tenants. A tenant calls about heating that has stopped working; the assistant talks them through checking the consumer unit, confirms their safety, books a repair appointment, and then recommends available properties, ending on a full property listing with photos and an enquiry button. The right-hand half of the screen is the tenant CRM and repair calendar, updating live as the call proceeds, which is what makes this worth showing: the assistant is writing into a system of record, not just talking.

chapters.label: A tenant calls about the heating
chapters.talkTrack: Left half is the tenant site and the voice assistant. Right half is the letting agent's CRM. Keep an eye on the right as the call goes on.

chapters.label: Booking the repair appointment
chapters.talkTrack: It identifies the tenant and their address, then books the repair. The appointment appears in the calendar on the right while you watch, which is the point: it is writing into the system, not taking a message.

chapters.label: Talking the tenant through the fuse box
chapters.talkTrack: This part is a genuine triage. It walks them to the consumer unit, gets the power back, and then tells them when to treat it as unsafe and call the emergency line. A lot of repair calls end here and never need a visit.

chapters.label: Recommending available properties
chapters.talkTrack: Then it switches job entirely, from maintenance to lettings, and starts matching available properties to what they want.

chapters.label: The property listing
chapters.talkTrack: And it ends on a full listing, photos and an enquiry button. Same assistant, two completely different business processes.

chapters.label: A day in the life
chapters.talkTrack: It is framed as a day in the life rather than a feature tour, which makes it easier to follow if you are not already living in these dashboards.

chapters.label: Per-agent metrics at a glance

chapters.label: The manager dashboard

chapters.label: The agent's own view
chapters.talkTrack: This is the part people forget to ask about. The agent sees their own numbers, so performance management is not something done to them out of sight.

chapters.label: KPI trends and coaching events

talkingPoints: Structured as a day in the life across manager and agent roles rather than as a feature tour
Per-agent metrics include AI usage alongside traditional measures like handle time and active time
Agents can see their own performance, not just their supervisor
Coaching events are plotted against KPI trends, so the effect of coaching is visible

assets.title: Energy: a move-home chat, self-service through to wrap-up
assets.summary: The cleanest end-to-end chat demo in the set, on a fictional energy retailer called NiCE Energy & Utilities. A customer moving home talks to a virtual assistant called Buzz about final meter readings and changing their address, then the conversation escalates to a human agent who has Copilot alongside them in App Space: a transfer summary so they arrive with context, live sentiment, suggested replies, and knowledge articles for exactly these tasks. It ends properly, with the wrap-up generating the interaction summary automatically and the agent rating Copilot. Silent, so it needs narrating.

chapters.label: The energy site and Buzz
chapters.talkTrack: A fictional energy supplier, and the assistant has a name and a character. Small thing, but it is a decision a utility brand gets to make.

chapters.label: Meter readings and moving home
chapters.talkTrack: Two of the highest-volume utility contacts, handled in self-service: a final meter reading and a change of address.

chapters.label: Handover to a human agent
chapters.talkTrack: Now the agent side. Note they open with a transfer summary, so they are not asking the customer to start again.

chapters.label: Copilot: sentiment, replies, knowledge
chapters.talkTrack: This right-hand panel is App Space. Sentiment on the conversation, a suggested reply, and the knowledge articles for a final meter reading and an address change.

chapters.label: Wrap-up and the auto summary
chapters.talkTrack: The wrap-up is worth showing. The summary is generated when the interaction ends, so the agent is not typing notes.

chapters.label: Rating Copilot
chapters.talkTrack: And it closes with the agent rating Copilot, which is how the feedback loop gets its data.

chapters.talkTrack: Conversation on the left, Cognigy flow on the right, verifying who they are.

chapters.label: Secure card capture
chapters.talkTrack: A card capture step inside the conversation. Worth showing to anyone who assumes a chatbot cannot be in a payment path.

chapters.label: The handover

chapters.label: Copilot and the capture form
chapters.talkTrack: Copilot suggesting the reply, and the structured form for the request.

chapters.label: Wrap-up
chapters.talkTrack: Generated summary and disposition to close.

assets.title: Financial services: the full digital journey, with the Cognigy build on screen
assets.summary: The fullest financial-services demo, ten minutes on a fictional wealth and lending brand called FinanceOne. A customer authenticates, views a portfolio, makes a secure card payment and asks about a pension transfer; the Cognigy flow editor sits beside the conversation for the first three minutes so you can watch the identity check, the knowledge lookup and the payment step actually fire. It then hands over to a human agent with a customer card showing recent interactions, Copilot suggesting replies, and a structured form to capture the transfer request. Silent, so it needs narrating. The shorter handover clip is a cut of this same demo.

chapters.label: FinanceOne, and the chat opens
chapters.talkTrack: A fictional wealth and lending brand. Note the compliance furniture on the page: regulated, encrypted, PCI. That framing matters for this audience.

chapters.label: The Cognigy flow, beside the conversation
chapters.talkTrack: This is the part a technical buyer wants. The flow on the right is the thing answering on the left, and you can watch the nodes execute.

chapters.label: Identity verification and the portfolio
chapters.talkTrack: Authentication first, then it reads back the portfolio. Real numbers from a real lookup, including a loss, which is a braver demo choice than it looks.

chapters.label: Knowledge lookup on the product question
chapters.talkTrack: The product question is answered from knowledge rather than generated, which in a regulated industry is the difference between usable and not.

chapters.label: Handover, and the customer card
chapters.talkTrack: Into the agent workspace. The customer information card carries their last interactions, so the agent has the history without asking for it.

chapters.label: Copilot on a pension transfer
chapters.talkTrack: Copilot suggesting replies on a genuinely complex topic, a pension transfer and the charge that applies to it.

chapters.label: Capturing the request on a form
chapters.talkTrack: And the structured capture. A regulated process needs the data in fields, not in free text, and Copilot is filling it from the conversation.

chapters.label: Wrap-up and disposition
chapters.talkTrack: Ends the same way the others do: generated summary, disposition, done.

assets.title: Financial services: the voice AI agent, with the build on screen
assets.summary: The FinanceOne journey on voice. A phone call runs on the left while the Cognigy flow and its live test panel run on the right, so you can see the voice agent authenticate the caller and work through their request before handing to a human agent in CXone with Copilot. Eight minutes, with real call audio. The natural pairing for the FSI chat demos when someone asks whether the same thing works on the phone.

chapters.label: The call, and the flow behind it
chapters.talkTrack: Phone call on the left, the flow driving it on the right. Same architecture as the chat demo, different channel.

chapters.label: Authenticating the caller
chapters.talkTrack: Identity verification over voice, which is the step every bank asks about first.

chapters.label: Working through the request
chapters.talkTrack: The agent handles the request itself here, with the knowledge lookups visible in the panel as it goes.

chapters.label: Into the CXone agent workspace
chapters.talkTrack: Handover. Note the agent gets the call and the context together.

chapters.label: Copilot on the call
chapters.talkTrack: Copilot working on a live voice interaction rather than on chat text, which is the harder of the two problems.

chapters.label: Disposition and wrap-up
chapters.talkTrack: And the close, with the disposition captured.

assets.title: Government: the citizen self-service half, on its own
assets.summary: The self-service half of the government benefits journey without the caseworker section, in four and a half minutes. Same fictional UK Work & Support Service: explaining the benefit, capturing an identity document with the camera, a handwritten signature, continuing the conversation over SMS, a one-time code, and an eligibility check. Use it when the audience only cares about the citizen-facing side. Silent, so it needs narrating. Read the governance note first: this file carries the clearest personal-data exposure in the set.

chapters.label: The service, and the assistant
chapters.talkTrack: Straight in on the citizen side. This clip never leaves it.

chapters.label: Explaining the benefit
chapters.talkTrack: The eligibility and taper explanation, in plain language.

chapters.label: Camera capture of a document
chapters.talkTrack: Camera or gallery, captured in the conversation.

chapters.label: Handwritten signature
chapters.talkTrack: And signed by hand on screen, with a clear and a submit.

chapters.label: Continuing over SMS
chapters.talkTrack: The conversation moves to SMS here, which is the channel a lot of this cohort actually uses.

chapters.label: The eligibility check
chapters.talkTrack: Four questions, and it tells them whether to bother. Better for both sides than an abandoned application.

assets.reviewedBy: Olivier Attia

assets.title: Government: a citizen benefits claim, self-service through to caseworker
assets.summary: The most complete public-sector demo, on a fictional department called the UK Work & Support Service. A citizen makes a benefits claim in chat and the demo works through the things that usually stop a public-service journey going digital: photographing an identity document with the phone camera, signing on screen by hand, verifying by one-time code, and answering an eligibility check before starting. It then hands over to a caseworker in CXone with Copilot and structured forms. Silent, so it needs narrating. The self-service half also exists as a shorter standalone clip.

chapters.label: A government service, and the assistant
chapters.talkTrack: A fictional department, styled the way a UK government service is styled. The assistant sits on the page rather than behind a phone number.

chapters.label: Explaining the benefit
chapters.talkTrack: It explains the benefit and how the taper works, which is exactly the kind of question that generates avoidable call volume.

chapters.label: Photographing an identity document
chapters.talkTrack: This is the first of the hard ones. The citizen photographs a document with their phone camera, in the conversation, with guidance on lighting and framing.

chapters.label: Signing by hand, on screen
chapters.talkTrack: And a handwritten signature, captured in the chat. Between this and the document, most of the reason these journeys stayed on paper is gone.

chapters.label: One-time code verification
chapters.talkTrack: Verification by one-time code before anything sensitive proceeds.

chapters.label: The eligibility check
chapters.talkTrack: Four questions to establish eligibility before the citizen invests fifteen minutes in an application they cannot complete. Worth calling out as a deflection story, not just a service one.

chapters.label: Handover to a caseworker
chapters.talkTrack: Then the caseworker side, with Copilot and the structured forms a statutory process needs.

chapters.label: Disposition and close
chapters.talkTrack: Generated summary, disposition, and Copilot feedback saved.

assets.reviewedBy: Olivier Attia

assets.title: Government: a voice AI agent, in English and Welsh
assets.summary: A citizen phones the fictional UK Work & Support Service about their State Pension and is handled by a voice AI agent, with the Cognigy flow visible beside the call. Two things make this the strongest public-sector clip in the set. The caller asks for the answer more slowly and in Welsh, and gets it, which in Wales is a statutory requirement rather than a nice-to-have. And it handles third-party authority, someone acting as a delegate on another person's claim. It closes by texting the citizen a link to continue online. Has real call audio.

chapters.label: The call, and the flow behind it
chapters.talkTrack: Voice call on the left, the flow on the right. The AI agent has a name and a role, which is how a public body would present it.

chapters.label: Explaining the benefit over voice
chapters.talkTrack: The same eligibility explanation as the chat demos, but spoken, which is harder: it has to be short enough to listen to.

chapters.label: Slower, and in Welsh
chapters.talkTrack: This is the moment to stop on. The caller asks for it more slowly and in Welsh, and gets it. For a UK public-sector audience that is a compliance answer, not a feature.

chapters.label: A signature, captured mid-journey
chapters.talkTrack: A signature comes back into the flow, so the voice journey is not limited to what can be said out loud.

chapters.label: Acting as a delegate
chapters.talkTrack: And third-party authority: someone helping their partner claim. Every public service has this case and most digital journeys ignore it.

chapters.label: Texting a link to continue online
chapters.talkTrack: It ends by sending a link so they can finish online, and closes the case. Channel switch as a deliberate outcome rather than a failure.

assets.reviewedBy: Olivier Attia

assets.title: Government: Copilot detecting a vulnerable citizen on a call
assets.summary: Three and a half minutes on the agent side of a government voice call, and the only asset in the room that shows vulnerability handling properly. Copilot flags a personal vulnerability from what the citizen says on the call, and the caseworker completes a vulnerability capture form: the category, whether consent was given to refer or escalate, and the contact details needed to act on it. It ends on the CRM record the case is written into. The best clip in the room for a public-sector or regulated buyer who asks about duty of care. Has real call audio.

chapters.label: The call arrives
chapters.talkTrack: The citizen is already speaking to the AI agent when this starts. This clip is the human half.

chapters.label: Copilot flags a vulnerability
chapters.talkTrack: Here is the point of the clip. Copilot has picked a vulnerability signal out of what was said and raised it, rather than leaving the agent to notice.

chapters.label: The vulnerability capture form
chapters.talkTrack: And then it is captured properly: the category, and crucially whether the citizen consented to a referral. That consent question is what makes this defensible rather than intrusive.

chapters.label: Contact details and next steps
chapters.talkTrack: Details captured so somebody can actually follow up.

chapters.label: The CRM record
chapters.talkTrack: It finishes on the record in the CRM. Worth showing to anyone who asks where this ends up, because a safeguarding flag that lives only in a transcript is no use.

assets.reviewedBy: Olivier Attia

assets.title: Healthcare: a patient journey across SMS, chat and the agent desk
assets.summary: Nine minutes on a fictional digital health provider, NiCE Healthcare, and the only demo in the room that spends its first three minutes inside a phone. A patient is handled over SMS with a verification code and an interactive list to pick a consultation type, then on web chat for a repeat prescription with an identity check and a choice of pharmacy collection or delivery, then by a human agent who checks a referral, advises the patient and books an appointment. Note before showing it: this file has no audio track at all, so it plays completely silent.

chapters.label: On the patient's phone
chapters.talkTrack: It opens on a phone rather than a website, which is right for healthcare: this cohort is not sitting at a desk.

chapters.label: Verification by code over SMS
chapters.talkTrack: A verification code over SMS. Note the demo even labels it as not a real message, which is the kind of care this content needs.

chapters.label: Choosing a consultation type
chapters.talkTrack: An interactive list rather than free text: standard, long, or urgent same-day. Structured choices are safer than open questions in a clinical context.

chapters.label: A repeat prescription in web chat
chapters.talkTrack: Now on web chat, for a repeat prescription. It verifies identity by date of birth before it will discuss medication.

chapters.label: Pharmacy collection or delivery
chapters.talkTrack: And it completes the task, including where the prescription goes. That is a whole call avoided.

chapters.label: The agent picks up
chapters.talkTrack: The human side, with the patient record and a summary of the last interaction already on screen.

chapters.label: Referral status and booking
chapters.talkTrack: Checking a referral and booking the appointment. These are the two things patients chase most, so it is a well-chosen ending.

chapters.label: Resolved
chapters.talkTrack: Dispositioned as resolved, with positive sentiment recorded.

assets.title: Telecom: a billing enquiry and a payment plan for a struggling customer
assets.summary: Four minutes on a fictional business telco, YourTelco, laid out as a split screen with the agent desktop on the left and the customer's own browser on the right, so you see both sides at once. The AI agent presents roaming plans as rich cards, then the conversation escalates: the customer is struggling to pay. Copilot raises a potential vulnerability and puts the required process on screen, and the agent sets up a payment plan on a structured form with a vulnerability flag. chapters.label: Both sides at once
chapters.talkTrack: The layout is the useful thing here: agent desktop on the left, what the customer sees on the right. Good for explaining the handover without switching screens.

chapters.label: Roaming plans as rich cards
chapters.talkTrack: Plans presented as cards with prices and inclusions, so the customer can compare rather than be read a list.

chapters.label: Escalation to a human
chapters.talkTrack: The conversation turns to the bill, and it hands over.

chapters.label: Copilot flags a potential vulnerability
chapters.talkTrack: Copilot raises a potential vulnerability and, importantly, puts the process the agent has to follow on the screen. For a regulated collections conversation that is the whole point.

chapters.label: Setting up the payment plan
chapters.talkTrack: A structured payment plan: the reason for the difficulty, the vulnerability flag, and the duration. Captured as data, so it is auditable.

chapters.label: Disposition and auto summary
chapters.talkTrack: Dispositioned, with the summary generated after the interaction ends.

chapters.talkTrack: And here is the interesting move. Rather than reading tariffs down the phone, it sends a link.

chapters.talkTrack: The customer is now comparing plans on their own screen while still on the call. Voice for the conversation, screen for the comparison, which is what each is actually good at.

assets.title: Proactive Outreach and outbound compliance
assets.summary: How compliance is enforced across an outbound programme, shown in the SmartReach admin: per-state calling windows, do-not-dial and do-not-leave-message settings, contact frequency rules such as one call per seven days in New York with lockout periods, and campaign segmentation. The last third shows the outbound voice AI agent being built and live test-called in Cognigy.

chapters.label: The question that decides it
chapters.talkTrack: It opens on the question that usually determines whether an outbound programme scales or stalls: how is compliance actually enforced, rather than merely intended.

chapters.label: Calling windows and do-not-contact
chapters.talkTrack: This is the SmartReach admin. Per state and area code: the permitted calling window, whether the number may be dialled at all, and whether you are allowed to leave a message. All configuration, no code.

chapters.label: Contact rules and frequency caps
chapters.talkTrack: Here is a specific rule: one call per seven days in New York, scoped by channel, with a lockout period afterwards. This screen is usually what an auditor actually wants to see.

chapters.label: Positioning
chapters.talkTrack: A positioning slide rather than product. Say the word and I will skip ahead to the build.

chapters.label: Segmentation and campaigns
chapters.talkTrack: Segmentation decides who gets contacted, on which channel, under which campaign. This is where contact strategy stops being a spreadsheet.

chapters.label: Building the AI agent that makes the calls
chapters.talkTrack: This is the part most people do not expect in an outbound video. That is Cognigy, and this is the outbound voice AI agent being built and then live test-called: its instructions, its memory handling, its grounding knowledge and its tool calls are all visible.

chapters.label: Scaling
chapters.talkTrack: It closes on the scale argument, which is the point of putting compliance in configuration rather than in each campaign.

talkingPoints: Compliance controls are configuration in the SmartReach admin, not per-campaign custom work
Shows per-state calling windows, do-not-dial and do-not-leave-message controls
Shows contact frequency rules with channel scope and lockout periods, at a granularity auditors ask about
Shows campaign segmentation driving channel selection
Shows a Cognigy AI agent authored and live test-called as the outbound voice agent, including grounding and tool calls
On-screen data is a demo environment, not a customer benchmark

assets.title: Quality Auto Scoring and GenAI Evaluation at Scale
assets.summary: Session on automating quality management: scoring every interaction and evaluating with generative AI rather than sampling.

assets.title: Resolve Problems Before They Arise with Proactive AI Agents
assets.summary: Session on proactive engagement: reaching customers before they have to contact you.

assets.title: Screen Intelligence: Beyond Transcripts
assets.summary: Session on using what happens on the agent desktop, not just the conversation transcript, as a signal for CX AI.

assets.title: Supervisor Workspace, managing human and AI agents
assets.summary: The supervisor experience for a mixed workforce of human and AI agents. An AI Agents view lists each bot like a team member with containment, quality score, sentiment and escalation rate, and flags conversations needing attention with the detected reason. Then live monitoring of a single conversation with transcript and generated summary, queue and SLA views, and reskill recommendations naming specific agents to activate when an SLA is at risk.

chapters.label: A mixed team
chapters.talkTrack: The setup is the real change: supervisors now manage human agents and AI agents in the same team. That is what breaks most existing supervisor tooling.

chapters.label: Supervising AI agents
chapters.talkTrack: This tab is the one that does not exist in most platforms. AI agents listed like staff, each with containment, quality score, sentiment and escalation rate. You can manage a bot the way you manage a person.

chapters.label: Finding the AI agents that are failing
chapters.talkTrack: Look at the rows flagged critical, and at the reason column: customer frustration detected, repeated clarification requests, a loop detected in conversation. That is how you catch a badly behaving AI agent before your customers report it.

chapters.label: Live monitoring one conversation
chapters.talkTrack: Drilling into a single contact: the path the conversation took, the full transcript, and a generated live summary so the supervisor does not have to read it all. They can drop a comment straight in.

chapters.label: Queues, SLA and alerts
chapters.talkTrack: Back to familiar territory. Skills, SLA, wait times, with proactive alerts on the right rather than a dashboard you have to keep staring at.

chapters.label: Reskill recommendations
chapters.talkTrack: This is the most useful screen in the video. An SLA is at risk, and rather than just alerting, it has named three specific agents who could cover that skill, with a reason for each. The supervisor applies it in one click.

talkingPoints: Supervisors manage human and AI agents from one workspace
AI agents are measured individually on containment, quality, sentiment and escalation rate
Conversations needing attention are surfaced with a detected reason, such as a conversation loop or repeated clarification
Live monitoring includes the conversation path, transcript and a generated summary, with supervisor commenting
Reskill recommendations name specific agents and give a rationale, and can be applied directly
On-screen figures are a demo environment, not a customer benchmark

tours.title: Agents, supervisors, and outbound
tours.goal: The visitor understands that NiCE treats AI agents as part of the workforce: assisted by Copilot on the agent side, measured and coached like staff on the supervisor side, and governed by compliance configuration on the outbound side.

steps.narration: Let me start where most people feel the pain first: the agent's screen, and how much admin sits around a single conversation.
steps.checkIn: How much of that after-call and mid-call admin do your agents do by hand today?

steps.narration: Now the layer above it. Once AI agents are handling real conversations, someone has to supervise them, and that is where most platforms have nothing to offer.
steps.checkIn: Do you have any way today to tell whether a bot is performing badly, other than customers complaining?

steps.narration: Last one, and this is the one your risk and compliance people will care about most. It also shows the AI agent itself being built, so it doubles as the technical view.
steps.checkIn: Would it help to go deeper on the compliance configuration with one of our specialists?
